walkthroughs.body_html:
Issues & Impact — a core area of GCSE Computer Science.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Issues & Impact brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Issues & Impact.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which technique involves breaking a problem into smaller sub-problems?
options: Abstraction
Decomposition
Iteration
Encapsulation

mcqs.q: What is the purpose of a trace table?
options: To compile code
To track variable values during execution
To draw a flowchart
To store program output

mcqs.q: Why are passwords stored as hashes rather than plaintext?
options: Hashes are encryption that can be decrypted with the right key.
Hashes compress the data to save space.
11 (counting the 1s).
Hashes are one-way - even an attacker who steals them cannot easily recover passwords.

mcqs.q: What is the denary value of binary 10110?
options: 10110 (treating it as a denary number).
Hashes compress the data to save space.
11 (counting the 1s).

mcqs.q: What is hexadecimal A in denary?
options: Hashes compress the data to save space.
26 (A's position in the alphabet).
1 (treating A as the first letter).

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Abstraction”?
options: Diagram using standardised shapes (oval, rectangle, diamond) to represent the flow of an algorithm.
Table used to track the changing values of variables as an algorithm executes step by step.
Removing unnecessary detail from a problem to focus on the essential features.
A finite, ordered sequence of unambiguous steps that solves a problem or completes a task.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Flowchart”?
options: Removing unnecessary detail from a problem to focus on the essential features.
Diagram using standardised shapes (oval, rectangle, diamond) to represent the flow of an algorithm.
A finite, ordered sequence of unambiguous steps that solves a problem or completes a task.
Structured English-like description of an algorithm, independent of any programming language.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Algorithm”?
options: Structured English-like description of an algorithm, independent of any programming language.
A finite, ordered sequence of unambiguous steps that solves a problem or completes a task.
Removing unnecessary detail from a problem to focus on the essential features.
Diagram using standardised shapes (oval, rectangle, diamond) to represent the flow of an algorithm.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Trace table”?
options: Removing unnecessary detail from a problem to focus on the essential features.
Breaking a complex problem into smaller, more manageable sub-problems.
Diagram using standardised shapes (oval, rectangle, diamond) to represent the flow of an algorithm.
Table used to track the changing values of variables as an algorithm executes step by step.

options: Structured English-like description of an algorithm, independent of any programming language.
Removing unnecessary detail from a problem to focus on the essential features.
Breaking a complex problem into smaller, more manageable sub-problems.

options: Removing unnecessary detail from a problem to focus on the essential features.

mcqs.q: How many distinct shapes are commonly used in basic flowcharts (start/end, process, decision, input/output)?
options: 4 shapes
6 shapes
5 shapes
